source_purpose.locator: cached PDF page 1; native text slice
source_purpose.quote:
This study presents a method to identify and rank potential sites for soil and water conservation tech-
niques. The method takes into account environmental site assessment criteria and a decision-making
method known as the Analytic Hierarchy Process. Spatial data is processed by applying a geographic
information system and potential sites are ranked by a multi-criteria evaluation based on meteorologic,
hydrologic, topographic, agronomic and pedologic criteria. The method is applied to identify potential
sites for terraces and bund systems in the Ronquillo watershed, located in the northern Andes of Peru.

supporting_native_excerpts.locator: cached PDF page 4; native text slice
supporting_native_excerpts.quote:
Because rainfall is fairly concentrated within the study area in the
rainy season and occurs almost daily, CN values for ACR III, which
are more representative for wet periods and thus higher ante-
cedent soil moisture, are chosen.
It is important to note that the SCS-CN method is only applicable
to single storm events (Ponce & Hawkins, 1996), so that it is inap-
propriate to use cumulated rainfall data, such as annual or season
means, in Eq. (1). However, the limiting temporal resolution of
three out of ﬁve rain gauges used in the present study hinders the
analysis of single rainfall events. To overcome this restraint, the
33%-exceedance probability of maximum daily rainfall is used to
model a single storm event.

supporting_native_excerpts.locator: cached PDF page 4; native text slice
supporting_native_excerpts.quote:
Topographic data is provided by a digital elevation model (DEM)
of the ASTER sensor system. The DEM has a spatial resolution of
30  30 m. The slope angle for each cell is calculated with the
Spatial Analyst tool within the ArcGIS environment. The cell size of
the
DEM
deﬁnes
the
spatial
resolution
of
the
subsequent
computations.

supporting_native_excerpts.locator: cached PDF page 5; native text slice
supporting_native_excerpts.quote:
The resulting map in Fig. 4A compiles the direct runoff in mm for
each raster cell within the Ronquillo watershed, which corresponds
to the altitude-dependent design rainfall, deﬁned as the 33%-ex-
ceedance probability of maximum daily rainfall. On the basis of the
direct runoff map as obtained by the SCS-CN method spatial runoff
coefﬁcients are computed as the ratio of direct runoff and the
design rainfall (Fig. 4B).

supporting_native_excerpts.locator: cached PDF page 5; native text slice
supporting_native_excerpts.quote:
The results show that for a large area of the Ronquillo watershed
the runoff coefﬁcient ranges between 0.33 and 0.66 (Fig. 4B). This
ﬁnding is in good accordance with runoff coefﬁcients of 0.23e0.60
during the rainy season (Jan.eApr.), as reported by Krois, Schulte,
Abendroth, and Schneider (2013), who delineated monthly runoff
coefﬁcients on the basis of rainfall and runoff data for the Ronquillo
River basin.

supporting_native_excerpts.locator: cached PDF page 7; native text slice
supporting_native_excerpts.quote:
Each criterion presented in Table 4 (rainfall, runoff coefﬁcient,
slope, land use, soil texture and soil depth) is rated according to its
boundary conditions, derived by literature survey (Bekele et al.,
2009; Critchley & Siegert, 1991; Hudson, 1987; Kahinda et al.,
2008; Mbilinyi et al., 2007; Oweis et al., 1999; Tumbo et al.,
2006). The suitability rating is transformed into an SL, scaling
from 1 to 9, thus expressing a suitability rating from ‘not suitable’ to
‘optimally suitable’. One should note that the SL for terraces and
bunds are identical except for the criterion slope. The latter are
more appropriate on moderate slopes (<5), whereas terraces are
optimally suitable on steep slopes (18e30). The suitability of each
criterion with respect to the corresponding SWCT is visualized in
the form of criteria maps (Fig. 8).

retained_profile.quantity: Modelled event direct runoff divided by design rainfall (Q/P)
retained_profile.input_method: SCS-CN; wet antecedent runoff condition III; 33%-exceedance probability of maximum daily rainfall used as design storm.
retained_profile.direction: Increasing suitability rank with increasing modelled event runoff coefficient for terraces and bunds in the source site-selection model.
retained_profile.boundary_ambiguity: Shared endpoints 0.3 and 0.6 are printed in adjacent ranges without an inclusion convention; >0.9 is explicit, and 0.9 is the printed upper edge of the highly suitable interval. Do not silently set .9 to optimum or infer interpolation.

importance.meaning: AHP source criterion weights, not calibrated response scores or approved runtime MCDA weights.

retained_profile.source_scope: Terraces and bunds, Ronquillo watershed, northern Peru. Existing EV and target mapping are terracing only; this proposal does not add bund-family applicability.
retained_profile.lineage: Source attributes boundary classes collectively to earlier manuals/studies; not independently estimated ecological transitions. Keep primary-source lineage unresolved rather than assign a specific cited source to the runoff classes.

numeric_plausibility.measurement: 30m grid; model-derived storm Q/P, not observed annual runoff or CN. Source comparison with monthly coefficients is contextual concordance, not validation of the >0.9 suitability class.
numeric_plausibility.precision: Classes 0.3 wide, unlike the previously flagged 20mm rainfall band. No uncertainty estimates or validation of the ranking transitions found in the inspected methods/results/discussion.
numeric_plausibility.meaning: Source genuinely uses the classes for spatial implementation ranking. Benefits/need motivation is context, not evidence the whole claim belongs outside T4. >0.9 is a source preference class, not a survival threshold or universal requirement.
numeric_plausibility.calibration: Singleton opt_low loses three retained ranks and explicit > boundary. Shared endpoints and conversion of source 3/5/7/9 into runtime scores need an explicit synthesis decision. Source does not report a runoff exclusion.
numeric_plausibility.transfer: Preserve entire regional quantitative profile for compatible source comparison; do not pool with CN, runoff depth or annual runoff coefficients. CN is derived from land-cover/soil inputs also entering other criteria; assess overlap before independent weighting.
